# OpenCode CLI evidence (ADR-022)

`run-help.txt` is a **captured, real `opencode run --help`**, not a
hand-authored example. `TestOpenCodeArgvMatchesCapturedHelp` in
`../../opencode_test.go` reads it and fails when a flag the adapter emits is not
an option of the captured CLI, when a value the adapter passes is not one of
that option's declared choices, or when a flag the adapter must never emit stops
being a real option (the forbidden list would then be guarding nothing).

`capture.sh` regenerates both files and applies the redaction described in its
header. Re-capture when the version policy raises the tested OpenCode version,
and update the table below in the same change.

## What was captured

| Field       | Value                                                                       |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Host OS     | macOS 27.2 (Darwin 27.2.0, arm64)                                           |
| Captured at | 2026-11-14                                                                  |
| Command     | `opencode run --help`, stdin from `/dev/null`                               |
| Stream      | stdout; stderr is empty (1.x printed it on stderr). `capture.sh` keeps both |
| CLI version | `2.2.7` (`opencode --version` prints `opencode v2.2.7`, `version.txt`)      |
| Install     | `https://opencode.ai/v2/install --version 2.2.7`                            |
| Exit code   | 0                                                                           |
| Redaction   | `capture.sh`; nothing needed redacting                                      |

## Pinned models catalog (#3315)

`../../opencode-models-catalog.json.gz` is the models catalog OpenCode 2.2.7
bundles: the document it reads when `OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH` names no file and
nothing is cached, before it would fetch models.dev. Every run and probe hands
OpenCode a copy through `OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH`, and `openCodeCatalogEnv` and
`openCodeAnthropicModels` are derived from it.

| Field       | Value                                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CLI version | `2.2.7`                                                                 |
| Captured at | 2026-11-17, on the host above                                           |
| Source      | `/$bunfs/root/snapshot-czv35j7j.txt` in the binary's Bun module graph   |
| Content     | 233 providers, each with `env`; UTF-16LE in the binary, stored as UTF-8 |
| Stored      | `gzip -9 -n` (8,247,427 bytes of JSON, sha256 `3ea43e2d…494aea33`)      |

To re-capture for a new max-tested version:

1. Read the Bun trailer at the end of the binary (`\n---- Bun! ----\n`). The
   32 bytes before it are the offsets: a `u64` payload size, then the module
   table as a `u32` offset and length. The payload starts at
   `trailer - 32 - size`.
2. Each module table entry is 52 bytes and starts with the name and the
   contents, each a `u32` offset and length. Find the entry whose name is
   `/$bunfs/root/snapshot-*.txt`, and decode its contents from UTF-16LE.
3. Write the JSON as UTF-8, `gzip -9 -n` it over the embedded file, re-derive
   both maps (the unit tests print the entries to paste), and raise
   `openCodeCatalogVersion`.
4. Run the `opencode_integration` tests in `opencode_catalog_integration_test.go`
   against the new binary. They check that the pinned file lists the same
   models as the bundled catalog, and that the binary reads the file (a model
   dropped from a copy disappears). They also check that each catalog
   variable, set alone, loads only the providers the policy binds it to. That
   last check found the one code binding 2.2.7 adds, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` to
   `cloudflare-workers-ai` (`openCodeCodeBoundEnv`).

## OpenCode 2.2.7 stream captures (#3305)

Real `opencode run --standalone --format json` stdout from 2.2.7, captured
2026-11-16 on the host above. Each run used a throwaway `HOME`, the four XDG
roots and `env -i`, with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1` and
`OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1`, under a perl `alarm` in its own process group.
The provider was a loopback OpenAI-compatible stub with a placeholder key.
Every stream went through `../../../testdata/redact-opencode.jq`: session ids
became placeholders and scratch paths became `/tmp/nightgauge-fixture`. Only
stub text remains in the provider messages. `stream_test.go`,
`opencode_retry_watchdog_test.go` and `opencode_tool_evidence_test.go` in
`internal/execution`, and `opencode_evidence_test.go` in this package, parse them.

| Fixture                        | Run                                                                                                   | Exit                    |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `stream-no-route.jsonl`        | `-m stub/nope`: one `error` event, `error.type` `provider.no-route`                                   | 1                       |
| `stream-retry-internal.jsonl`  | Stub answers HTTP 500: `step_start`, then `retry` attempts 2–6 with `error.type` `provider.internal`  | killed by alarm at 35 s |
| `stream-retry-transport.jsonl` | `baseURL` on a closed port: `retry` attempts 2–6 with `error.type` `provider.transport`               | killed by alarm at 35 s |
| `stream-tool-state.jsonl`      | `read` completed, `shell` rejected under `"bash":"ask"`, `read` of a missing file failed, then `stop` | 0                       |
| `stream-subagent.jsonl`        | A `subagent` call (agent `general`) that completed, then `stop`                                       | 0                       |

What the captures show:

- `retry` carries top-level `attempt` (2 on the first retry), `nextRetryAt` (epoch ms)
  and `error` {`type`, `message`, and for an HTTP error `status` and `response.body`}.
  Attempts 2–6 arrived about 2, 4, 8 and 11 s apart, so the fifth retry lands about
  24 s in. The `provider.transport` message carried no URL.
- A tool call's `part.state` has `metadata.providerCall` and `metadata.providerResult`,
  each `{"executed": false}` for every local tool. They say whether the provider ran
  the tool, not whether it ran at all. `state.error` is still a string.
- A headless `ask` rejection's error is "This non-interactive run cannot ask the user
  for permission, so the request was rejected. Continue without this action." stderr
  got one ANSI line: `! permission requested: shell (…); auto-rejecting`.
- The subagent's session id is in `part.state.metadata.metadata.sessionID`.

### Descendant-session usage on 2.2.7

Re-verified against the data directory of the `stream-subagent.jsonl` run, with the
commands the usage fold (`internal/execution/opencode_usage.go`) runs:

| Fold step                                                       | Observed on 2.2.7                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `opencode db "<openCodeSessionTreeQuery>" --format json --pure` | Fails, exit 1: there is no `db` subcommand. `--format` and `--pure` are "Unrecognized flag"                                                                                                                       |
| `opencode export <session> --sanitize --pure`                   | Fails, exit 1: there is no top-level `export`, and `--pure` does not exist                                                                                                                                        |
| `opencode session export <session> --sanitize`                  | Fails, exit 1: without `--standalone` it reaches for the managed background service ("Managed service port … is already in use")                                                                                  |
| `opencode session export --standalone --sanitize <session>`     | Exit 0. `info` has `id`, `tokens`, `cost`, `model`, `outcome`, `location`, `projectID`, `time` and `title`. `info.tokens` is still `{input, output, reasoning, cache {read, write}}`, and `info.cost` is a number |
| Session tree in `<data>/opencode/opencode.db`                   | The table is `session_v2`, not `session`. It keeps `parent_id`, and the child's row names the parent. It also holds `tokens_*` and `cost` columns                                                                 |
| Parent vs child usage                                           | Parent `info.tokens` 30 in / 6 out (its two steps, 20/4, plus a title request). Child 20/4 (its two steps). The parent does not include the child's usage, so a fold must still add each descendant               |

So the token shape `sessionUsage` reads is unchanged, but neither command the fold
runs exists on 2.x. On 2.2.7 the fold records drift markers and a partial usage
result. Porting the fold (`session export --standalone`, plus a way to list
descendants without `db`) is recorded as discovered work from #3305.

## Behaviour observed on 1.18.30

These observations were made on OpenCode 1.18.30, before the 2.x capture
above. The OpenCode 2.x port (epic #3196) re-observes each one; until then the
`opencode_integration` suites that assert them skip on 2.x and name the issue
that ports them.

ADR-022 rests on behaviour, not only on flags, so the observations it cites were
made on 1.18.30, the same day unless a row gives a later date. Each run
used a throwaway directory for all four XDG base directories, a scratch git
repository as `--dir`, and a stub OpenAI-compatible model server on
`127.0.0.1` that recorded every request and returned canned replies, so no
hosted provider and no operator configuration was involved. Every invocation
was bounded with `perl -e 'alarm 90; exec @ARGV'`.
The provider-block rows also used a throwaway `HOME` and an environment cleared
with `env -i`, in which every API-key variable held a fake sentinel value, never
a real key. The run-isolation rows (#1616) also used a throwaway `HOME` and
`env -i`, and ran under a macOS sandbox profile that refused every outbound
connection except loopback. The per-run config rows (#1625) used a throwaway
`HOME` and `env -i` as well, and ran only `debug config` and `models`, so no
model request was sent. The steering and MCP rows (#1626) dispatched through
`Manager.RunStage` with a throwaway `HOME`, to the #1618 stub provider on
`127.0.0.1` behind a front that kept each request's system messages in memory,
or ran only `debug config` in the stage's environment.

| Observation                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | How it was observed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Piped stdin with no positional message becomes the user message verbatim; exit 0                                                                                                                                                     | A marker string piped to `opencode run --format json ...` arrived as the `user` message in the stub's recorded request                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
